P2A00.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Range/Performance Bank 1 Sensor 1
P2A00.description: O2 Sensor Circuit Range/Performance Bank 1 Sensor 1: the signal is implausible or outside the valid range.

causes.label: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2A01.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Range/Performance Bank 1 Sensor 2
P2A01.description: The rear oxygen sensor on bank 1 does not show the expected slow steady-state behaviour after the catalyst. Either the sensor is degraded or the catalyst itself behaves abnormally.

causes.label: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2A02.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Range/Performance Bank 1 Sensor 3
P2A02.description: The optional third oxygen sensor on bank 1 (typically downstream of a second catalyst) returns implausible values during long-term monitoring.

causes.label: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2A03.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Range/Performance Bank 2 Sensor 1
P2A03.description: The front oxygen sensor on bank 2 reacts too slowly or shows insufficient signal swing during closed-loop fuel control.

causes.label: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2A04.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Range/Performance Bank 2 Sensor 2
P2A04.description: The rear oxygen sensor on bank 2 shows abnormal behaviour during long-term plausibility evaluation. Often a sign of an aged sensor or weakened catalyst.

causes.label: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2A05.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Range/Performance Bank 2 Sensor 3
P2A05.description: The third oxygen sensor on bank 2 (after a second catalyst stage on some vehicles) returns implausible values. Often related to sensor aging or mechanical exhaust leak upstream.

causes.label: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2A06.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Range/Performance Bank 1 Sensor 4
P2A06.description: The fourth oxygen sensor on bank 1, where present, returns implausible values during long-term plausibility evaluation. Used on multi-stage aftertreatment systems.

causes.label: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2A07.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Range/Performance Bank 2 Sensor 4
P2A07.description: The fourth oxygen sensor on bank 2 returns values outside the expected long-term performance window during plausibility checks.

causes.label: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2A08.title: O2 Sensor Negative Voltage Bank 1 Sensor 3
P2A08.description: The ECM detects a negative voltage on the signal line of oxygen sensor 3 on bank 1. This is unusual for narrow-band sensors and often indicates a short to a negative reference, ground offset, or a wide-band sensor wired incorrectly.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to negative reference
Ground offset between sensor and ECM

P2A09.title: O2 Sensor Negative Voltage Bank 2 Sensor 1
P2A09.description: The ECM detects a negative voltage on the signal line of oxygen sensor 1 on bank 2. This is unusual for narrow-band sensors and often indicates a short to a negative reference, ground offset, or a wide-band sensor wired incorrectly.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to negative reference
Ground offset between sensor and ECM

P2A0A.title: Manifold Absolute Pressure Sensor B Circuit
P2A0A.description: The ECM detects a generic fault on the secondary manifold absolute pressure sensor (MAP B). Air load estimation cannot be cross-checked.

P2A0B.title: Manifold Absolute Pressure Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P2A0B.description: The MAP B signal does not correlate with TPS, MAF, or RPM as expected. Vacuum leak, restricted port, or sensor drift.

causes.label: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2A0C.title: Manifold Absolute Pressure Sensor B Circuit Low
P2A0C.description: Voltage on the MAP B signal line is below the expected window. Wire shorted to ground or sensor short.

causes.label: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2A0D.title: Manifold Absolute Pressure Sensor B Circuit High
P2A0D.description: Voltage on the MAP B signal line is above the expected window. Wire shorted to B+ or sensor open. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.label: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2A0E.title: Manifold Absolute Pressure Sensor B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P2A0E.description: The MAP B signal drops out or jumps intermittently. Loose connector or noisy ground reference. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.label: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P2A0F.title: Fuel Supply Heater Performance
P2A0F.description: The fuel supply heater does not raise fuel temperature within the calibrated time window. Common in diesel and biofuel installations to prevent paraffin or fat crystallisation in cold weather.

P2A10.title: O2 Sensor Negative Voltage Bank 2 Sensor 2
P2A10.description: The ECM detects a negative voltage on the signal line of oxygen sensor 2 on bank 2. This is unusual for narrow-band sensors and often indicates a short to a negative reference, ground offset, or a wide-band sensor wired incorrectly.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to negative reference
Ground offset between sensor and ECM

P2A11.title: O2 Sensor Negative Voltage Bank 2 Sensor 3
P2A11.description: The ECM detects a negative voltage on the signal line of oxygen sensor 3 on bank 2. This is unusual for narrow-band sensors and often indicates a short to a negative reference, ground offset, or a wide-band sensor wired incorrectly.

P2A3E.title: Alternative Fuel Delivery Error

P2A3F.title: Excessive Time to Enter Alternative Fuel Control

P2A40.title: Alternative Fuel System - Injector Leakage to Rail Detected
